environmentalPersistence: Low — rapidly degraded by light and soil microbes; half-life hours to days

lowDose.description: Adaptive stress response — stomatal closure conserves water, seed dormancy maintained, appropriate senescence induction. Protective under drought. Mild defense priming.

highDose.description: Forced premature senescence, strong stomatal closure blocking photosynthesis, accelerated chlorophyll degradation, leaf abscission, growth arrest, enhanced ethylene production.

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Moderate-strong — ABA inhibits cell elongation and division broadly
morphologicalEffects.leafCurl: Moderate — stomatal closure combined with early senescence causes structural changes
morphologicalEffects.wilting: Paradoxical — ABA closes stomata to PREVENT wilting under drought; exogenous ABA causes apparent wilting at high dose by disrupting normal water balance
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Moderate-strong at high dose — premature chlorophyll degradation
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Moderate — premature senescence progresses to necrosis
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Mildly reduced — ABA inhibits root cell elongation
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Old leaves most affected — ABA-driven senescence proceeds oldest-first

physiologyEffects.photosyntheticRate: Strongly reduced — stomatal closure blocks CO₂ entry
physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Very strongly reduced — ABA is THE primary stomatal closure signal
physiologyEffects.waterUptake: Maintained or improved at low dose (drought response); impaired at high dose
physiologyEffects.nutrientTransport: Disrupted at high dose via reduced transpiration stream

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Moderate — ABA induces ROS burst as signaling molecule (intentional)

microbiomeEffects.diversityReduction: Mild — ABA alters root exudate composition moderately
microbiomeEffects.beneficialBacteriaEffect: Near-normal — ABA modulates rhizosphere but doesn't strongly suppress PGPR
microbiomeEffects.fungalEffect: Mycorrhizal associations maintained — ABA promotes mycorrhizal colonization under stress

temporalDynamics.firstSymptomsHours: 1–6 hours for stomatal closure (fastest stomatal response of all hormones); 24–72 hours for visible morphological changes
temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: 1–2 weeks — ABA degrades quickly; stomata reopen within hours of removal
temporalDynamics.sensitization: Moderate — ABA can prime stress memory via epigenetic mechanisms

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Surface dullness (stomatal closure visible as matte surface); then yellowing; mild purple at high dose
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Stomatal surface (dullness/closure) — first visible change. Then old leaves yellow.
visualSimulation.damageSpread: Old-to-young progression — senescence proceeds from base upward
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Uniform stomatal surface change; patchy senescence on older leaves
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Moderate — ABA-GE and dehydrin signature; moderate compared to stress chemicals
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: Good — stomata reopen quickly; yellowing partially reversible; new growth healthy

synergies.synergyNote: ABA + ethylene is the canonical senescence acceleration combination — ABA initiates and ethylene amplifies; together they produce the fastest chlorophyll degradation in the simulator
synergies.antagonismNote: ABA opposes GA-mediated growth and seed germination; ABA opposes CK-mediated anti-senescence. The ABA/CK ratio determines leaf age and stress response intensity.

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Endogenous stress hormone — produced in roots and leaves under drought, cold, salinity, and pathogen stress; found universally in land plants
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Experimental drought-priming treatments; seed dormancy regulation; post-harvest delay (inhibits premature germination)
educationalContext.climateLink: ABA is the primary hormone mediating plant drought responses — as climate change increases drought frequency and intensity, ABA biology becomes central to crop improvement
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Both — produced naturally in all plants under stress
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: Why plants wilt and then recover when watered — ABA is the signal that says 'close your stomata, conserve water.' The fastest-acting hormone signal in the plant kingdom at just 1–6 hours.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Drought-tolerant crop development, climate adaptation, water use efficiency in agriculture
